meta.title: Layer 4 · Elasticsearch: who reaches it, and with which credentials

components.label: Kibana
components.explanation: In the demo, Kibana is not on the internal Elasticsearch network: its ELASTICSEARCH_HOSTS points at the proxy.

components.label: Index & ENRICH lookup
components.explanation: GET /_resolve/index turns aliases and wildcards into concrete names; GET /_enrich/policy finds the source indices of an ENRICH policy. Both use the proxy's API key.

components.label: Team indices
components.explanation: Read as the end user: the relay authenticates as proxy_service and sets es-security-runas-user, so Elasticsearch applies that user's own roles too.

components.label: System indices
components.explanation: Refused to every user unless a rule names them explicitly. Kibana's kibana_system account reaches them as a passthrough user.

components.label: Native realm
components.explanation: proxy_service holds only a run_as role. Each LDAP user has a native shadow user whose password is a secret shared by the proxy and the bootstrap only, so Kibana's profile activation works without the real LDAP password.

cards.title: Three credentials, three jobs
items: proxy_service (run_as): reads data as the caller
API key: resolves index names and ENRICH policies
kibana_system: Kibana's own system indices, outside the ACL

cards.title: No way around the proxy
items: Elasticsearch sits on an internal Docker network
Users' credentials are never forwarded to Elasticsearch
Kubernetes NetworkPolicy: planned with the Helm chart

items: Hidden index proxy-conversations: one doc per conversation, one per message
